reference.source: immutable git blobs, not concurrent working-tree changes

coverage.definition: Every tracked src/**/*.svelte and src/**/*.svelte.ts at reference.commit is a coverage unit, including reference harnesses and previews; reference-test-support is separately labelled, never silently subtracted. Other inventoried files are dependencies/boundaries, not additional view units. Count measures source accounting, not semantic or visual parity.
coverage.statusPolicy: unmigrated means no accepted source-to-target evidence in this snapshot. Implementation, visual parity and functional parity require separate reviewed evidence tied to source hash, target revision and states. Do not promote an entire source from one passing case.

methodology.scope: Exhaustive git-tree enumeration of Svelte view/reactivity modules plus all non-test UI, patterns, catalog, routes, direct framework adapters, bound selector owners and named cutover entry points. Supporting TS-only domain modules are traced by import family and existing owner, not claimed as view ports.
methodology.imports: Lexical import/from/dynamic-string-import scan of script blocks with comments discarded; resolves relative paths and repository aliases, re-exports and .svelte.ts extension convention. Family edges include type-only imports and are planning candidates, not proof of runtime reachability.
limitations: Computed dynamic imports and nonliteral import.meta.glob expansions need runtime/build review; preview glob is enumerated separately.
Test-support name/path classification is advisory; denominator includes every file so unusual harness names cannot hide a source.
Preview literal states are not catalog fixture state coverage; catalog manifests, renderer IDs and fixture lists are independent contracts.
No source execution, browser parity or product readiness is certified by this analysis.

findings.decision: Use one ReactStore in apps/react and one Svelte Store in the reference app. Existing configured-store extends Svelte Store and adds getReadableState; importing the old store is not framework-neutral reuse. Audit reducer/middleware dependency closure before sharing it.

The listed 125 selector modules call store.createSelector against the Svelte singleton. Preserve pure selector meaning and owning actions, but bind to the React runtime without importing the old selector singleton. Review transitive imports of slices and services; absence of a direct svelte import does not make a module safe.

Keep store initialization separate from app-saga startup. Sandbox must not start production watchers. React mount/unmount, development StrictMode and HMR must not duplicate subscriptions, timers or saga owners. Preserve disposal/bridge clearing and locale rerender behavior.

Replace SvelteKit navigation/environment/page adapters with TanStack Start/Router navigation and explicit browser capability. Retain settings return destination, deep-link query/hash, navigation cancellation and HUD no-navigation guard.

Notify takes Svelte Component/ComponentProps and svelte-sonner custom components; callers cannot carry this adapter into React. Preserve notification IDs, progress/update/dismiss and undo settlement semantics. Confirm queue is a candidate for reuse, but host rendering and focus restoration need React behavior verification.

Port Svelte context, rune helpers, DOM actions/transitions and TipTap node mount lifecycle. Share semantic CSS/motion data and framework-neutral editor extensions only after dependency review. Preserve terminal singleton/PTY ownership across remounts rather than constructing competing managers.

catalog.contract: Metadata fixtures and named .preview scene states are distinct denominators. Preserve both; renderer presence is not proof that all fixture states render. Resolve computed preview state maps through the reference browser API before generating parity cases.

panelTabTypes.contract: Preserve lazy import, cancellation/retry, width tier, renameability, workspace/layout IDs, header actions and inactive-tab retention. A TanStack Start/Router route per workspace must not remount retained browser/terminal/editor guests.

parallelism.ownership: One batch per source via sources[].batch. Apps/react target exports, router registration, root package/lock and parity inventory have single integration owners; feature agents request central registration changes instead of concurrent edits. Legacy source remains the reference.
parallelism.planningVsGraph: dependsOn is an integration DAG. families[].observedDependencies lists lexical type/value import edges, not hard task dependencies; metadata barrels and mutual UI composition create cycles. Freeze interfaces and integrate the full family before acceptance. Re-evaluate transitive runtime imports before sharing any module.
parallelism.splitting: Large families include reference harnesses. Split an oversized family by named user contract and exact source subset in the task note before delegating, preserving one owner per source. In particular panel-shell may split chrome/tab-registry from panel-canvas; chat-transcript may split streaming/scrollback from queued messages/agent cards; modals split workspace lifecycle from auth/integration dialogs.
parallelism.futureReferenceRefresh: Enumerate the same git-tree rule at the new reference SHA, compare path+sha256, add/remove/rename records explicitly, invalidate changed-source evidence and rerun affected state/journey cases. Do not carry accepted status across hash drift implicitly.
parallelism.assignableUnits: Delegate workUnits, whose exact sourcePaths partition every inventory row; batches are integration groups. Existing Svelte tests/harnesses stay reference-only, never copied as new mocked functional tests. A work unit does not authorize edits to another unit or shared registration files.

functionalJourneys.policy: No mocked unit/integration tests, transport/network stubs or assertions of CSS/class spelling. Local interactive fixture state may demonstrate a production component; seeded/mock domain scenes are reference visuals only and never real product evidence. Core is the routine functional gate; optional means slower or prerequisite-dependent execution, not optional migration coverage. Unavailable prerequisites remain pending with a named owner.

legacyReferenceWarning.decision: Keep legacy fixtures unchanged as Svelte reference. Inspect each preview setup dependency before reusing it; existing passing Svelte mock tests cannot be copied or counted as new functional evidence.

requirements: Keep existing main/preload IPC and daemon contracts unchanged. Generated preload comes from index.template.ts and generation scripts, not hand edits to index.ts.
React output must match renderer asset serving assumptions in app://workspaces with absolute paths and SPA fallback; preserve web profile output separation and authenticated loopback bridge.
Preserve production route filtering: sandbox/test routes stay development-only; dev-console and hud are production route entries but not ordinary feature-navigation promises.
Translate root boot/splash, Store/saga lifecycle, locale and shared windows/HUD behavior before switching packaged renderer entry.
Verify native menus/accelerators, clipboard/dialogs, multiwindow, deep links, Monaco workers, real terminal, browser webContents, screenshots and workspace-file media in actual Electron.
Keep Svelte reference and its tests until all source dispositions and visual/functional evidence are accepted. Final dependency/build cleanup is a separate coordinated cutover, not a first-wave task.
